import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Accordion" />

# Accordion

DOS-styled collapsible content sections with CRT phosphor expand animation.

The Accordion system provides two components: **Section** (individual collapsible panel)
and **AccordionFill** (multi-section group). Sections expand with a phosphor-bloom
animation and use CGA-authentic colors for hover and active states.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Accordion stories](/story/components-accordion--default-accordion) for live interactive examples.

## Components

The Accordion system is composed of two components:

| Component | Role | Example |
|-----------|------|---------|
| **Section** | Single collapsible panel with header and content | FAQ item, settings group |
| **AccordionFill** | Multi-section container, manages a collection of Sections | FAQ list, settings page |

### Section (standalone)

```tsx
<Section title="Expandable Section" defaultExpanded={false}>
  Content goes here...
</Section>
```

### AccordionFill (grouped)

```tsx
<AccordionFill
  sections={[
    { title: 'Section 1', content: 'First section content' },
    { title: 'Section 2', content: 'Second section content' },
    { title: 'Section 3', content: 'Third section content' },
  ]}
  defaultExpandedIndex={0}
/>
```

## States

### Default (Collapsed)

Section header displays the title with a chevron-down icon on the right.
Content is hidden. Border uses `--color-semantic-border-default`.

### Expanded

When expanded, the section border brightens to `--color-semantic-text-secondary`,
the header gains an accent background, and content slides in with the
`section-expand` keyframe animation over `--duration-normal` (200ms).

### Hover

Header background changes to `--color-semantic-background-accent` with
`--color-semantic-text-secondary` text color, giving a CRT warm-up feel.

### Active

Header background shifts to `--color-semantic-background-secondary` with
amber text (`--color-cga-amber`) and a phosphor text-shadow glow.

## Interaction Design

The chevron icon rotates 180 degrees on expand/collapse, animated over
`--duration-normal` with ease-in-out timing. Content enters with a
max-height + opacity animation simulating a phosphor bloom.

## Accessibility

- **Focus visible**: 2px box-shadow outline using `--color-semantic-border-focus`
- **High contrast**: Border widens to 3px, title gets bold weight, focus ring widens to 3px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: Icon rotation transition and content expand animation disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA**: `aria-expanded` set on the header button to indicate open/closed state
- **Keyboard**: Full keyboard navigation — header is a native `<button>` element

## API Reference

### Section Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | `string` | — | The title text displayed in the section header |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The content revealed when the section is expanded |
| `defaultExpanded` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the section is expanded on initial render |
| `isHovered` | `boolean` | `false` | Force the hover visual state (for Storybook demos) |
| `isActive` | `boolean` | `false` | Force the active visual state (for Storybook demos) |
| `onToggle` | `(isExpanded: boolean) => void` | — | Callback fired when the section is toggled |

### AccordionFill Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `sections` | `Array<{ title: string; content: string }>` | — | Array of section data objects |
| `defaultExpandedIndex` | `number` | `-1` | Index of the section expanded by default (-1 = none) |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Section border and content divider |
| `--color-semantic-background-primary` | Section background |
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Default text color |
| `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Content text and expanded header text |
| `--color-semantic-background-accent` | Hover and expanded header background |
| `--color-semantic-background-secondary` | Active header background |
| `--color-cga-amber` | Active state text color |
| `--color-cga-amber-glow` | Active state text-shadow glow |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline ring |
| `--duration-normal` | Expand animation and icon rotation (200ms) |
| `--spacing-2` | Gap between sections in AccordionFill |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-family-fallback` | Fallback font family |
| `--typography-font-size-base` | AccordionFill base font size |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Alert" />

# Alert

DOS-styled dismissible notification with CRT phosphor entrance animation.

The Alert displays contextual feedback messages with type-specific CGA colors and icons.
It enters with a phosphor-bloom animation — blurring from dim to full brightness — simulating
a CRT monitor warming up.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Alert stories](/story/components-alert--default) for live interactive examples.

## Types

Each type maps to a specific semantic role with its own CGA color and icon:

| Type | Color | Icon | Example |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| **Info** | Amber | Info | General information, tips |
| **Success** | Bright Green | Done | Completed actions, confirmations |
| **Warning** | Amber | Warning | Caution, potential issues |
| **Error** | Bright Red | Error | Failures, critical problems |

```tsx
<Alert type="info" title="Information">Helpful details here.</Alert>
<Alert type="success" title="Success">Operation completed.</Alert>
<Alert type="warning" title="Warning">Proceed with caution.</Alert>
<Alert type="error" title="Error">Something went wrong.</Alert>
```

## Sizes

Two size variants for different contexts:

| Size | Max Width | Padding | Layout | Content Area |
|------|-----------|---------|--------|--------------|
| `large` | 1020px | 16px | Column (stacked) | Title + description visible |
| `small` | 350px | 0 8px | Row (inline) | Title only, content hidden |

```tsx
<Alert size="large" type="info" title="Large Alert">
  Description text is visible in the large variant.
</Alert>
<Alert size="small" type="info" title="Compact Alert" />
```

## States

### Dismissible

When an `onClose` handler is provided, a close button (X icon) appears in the
header. The close button has 0.7 opacity at rest, brightening to full opacity on hover.

```tsx
<Alert type="info" title="Dismissible" onClose={() => console.log('closed')}>
  This alert can be dismissed.
</Alert>
```

### With Action Link

When an `onClickHere` handler is provided, a "Click here" action link appears
below the description text. The link gains a phosphor text-shadow glow on hover.

```tsx
<Alert type="warning" title="Action Required" onClickHere={() => navigate('/settings')}>
  Your settings need attention.
</Alert>
```

## Interaction Design

### Entrance Animation

The alert enters with a CRT phosphor bloom over `--duration-slow` (400ms):

```css
@keyframes alert-enter {
  from { opacity: 0; filter: blur(4px) brightness(0.3); }
  to   { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0) brightness(1); }
}
```

This simulates phosphors warming from dim to full brightness on a cold CRT.

### Close Button

The close icon uses a smooth opacity transition (`--duration-fast`, 100ms) on hover.

### Action Link

The "Click here" link gains a `text-shadow: 0 0 6px currentColor` glow on hover,
creating a subtle phosphor highlight effect.

## Accessibility

- **High contrast**: 2px solid border added, title gets bold weight, close button gets 3px focus outline, action link gets underline + bold via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: Entrance animation, close button transition, and link transition all disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA**: Close button has `aria-label="Close alert"`, action link has `aria-label="Click for more information"`, type icon has `aria-label` describing the alert type
- **Keyboard**: Close button is a native `<button>` with full keyboard access

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error'` | `'info'` | Alert type determining color and icon |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | Size variant controlling layout and max width |
| `title` | `string` | — | Title text displayed in the alert header |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Description content (hidden in small size) |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | — | Close button click handler (renders close button when provided) |
| `onClickHere` | `() => void` | — | Action link click handler (renders "Click here" link when provided) |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-alert-info` | Info variant background |
| `--color-semantic-alert-success` | Success variant background |
| `--color-semantic-alert-warning` | Warning variant background |
| `--color-semantic-alert-error` | Error variant background |
| `--color-cga-amber` | Info and warning text color |
| `--color-cga-bright-green` | Success text color |
| `--color-cga-bright-red` | Error text color |
| `--color-cga-amber-dim` | Message body text color |
| `--duration-slow` | Entrance animation duration (400ms) |
| `--duration-fast` | Close button and link transition (100ms) |
| `--spacing-4` | Large variant padding |
| `--spacing-2` | Small variant horizontal padding |
| `--spacing-1` | Large variant content gap |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-family-fallback` | Fallback font family |

## Origin

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Badge" />

# Badge

DOS-styled status indicator for labels, tags, and categorical metadata.

The Badge is an inline display element for status, priority, and category information.
It uses CGA-authentic outline colors per variant and supports an optional dot indicator
for live-status use cases.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Badge stories](/story/components-badge--all-variants) for live interactive examples.

## Variants

Each variant maps to a specific semantic role with CGA-authentic colors:

| Variant | Color | Border | Background | Example |
|---------|-------|--------|------------|---------|
| **Default** | Primary text | Default border | Secondary bg | Tags, labels |
| **Success** | Bright Green | Bright Green | Transparent | Online, complete, approved |
| **Warning** | Yellow | Yellow | Transparent | Pending, caution, medium priority |
| **Error** | Bright Red | Bright Red | Transparent | Offline, failed, high priority |
| **Info** | Bright Cyan | Bright Cyan | Transparent | Syncing, informational |
| **Accent** | Secondary text | Default border | Accent bg | Active, highlighted, featured |

```tsx
<Badge variant="default">Label</Badge>
<Badge variant="success">Online</Badge>
<Badge variant="warning">Pending</Badge>
<Badge variant="error">Offline</Badge>
<Badge variant="info">Syncing</Badge>
<Badge variant="accent">Active</Badge>
```

## Sizes

Two sizes for different contexts:

| Size | Font | Padding | Min Height | Gap |
|------|------|---------|------------|-----|
| `small` | 10px | 2px 6px | 18px | 4px |
| `medium` | 12px | 4px 8px | 22px | 6px |

```tsx
<Badge size="small">Small</Badge>
<Badge size="medium">Medium</Badge>
```

## States

### With Dot Indicator

When `dot` is enabled, a small circular indicator (6px) appears before the text.
The dot color matches the variant color, making it ideal for live status indicators.

```tsx
<Badge variant="success" dot>Online</Badge>
<Badge variant="error" dot>Offline</Badge>
<Badge variant="warning" dot>Away</Badge>
```

### Real-World Usage

Badges work well for priority levels, source labels, scope tags, and status indicators:

```tsx
{/* Priority */}
<Badge variant="error" size="small">High</Badge>
<Badge variant="warning" size="small">Medium</Badge>
<Badge variant="default" size="small">Low</Badge>

{/* Status */}
<Badge variant="success" dot size="small">Online</Badge>
<Badge variant="error" dot size="small">Offline</Badge>
```

## Accessibility

- **High contrast**: Border widens to 2px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: Transitions disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA**: Supports `aria-label` prop for accessible label override; dot indicator is `aria-hidden="true"`
- **Text**: Uppercase text with 0.05em letter-spacing for readability at small sizes
- **WCAG**: WCAG 2.1 AA compliant color contrast

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'info' \| 'accent'` | `'default'` | Color scheme mapped to semantic role |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | Badge dimensions |
| `dot` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a circular dot indicator before the text |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Badge label content |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible label override |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-background-secondary` | Default variant background |
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Default variant text and dot |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Default and accent variant border |
| `--color-cga-bright-green` | Success variant text, border, and dot |
| `--color-cga-yellow` | Warning variant text, border, and dot |
| `--color-cga-bright-red` | Error variant text, border, and dot |
| `--color-cga-bright-cyan` | Info variant text, border, and dot |
| `--color-semantic-background-accent` | Accent variant background |
| `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Accent variant text and dot |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-family-fallback` | Fallback font family |
| `--typography-font-weight-regular` | Base font weight |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Breadcrumb" />

# Breadcrumb

DOS-styled navigation trail with framework-agnostic link support.

The Breadcrumb renders a hierarchical path showing the user's current location
within the application. It supports custom separators (including DOS-style backslash paths),
an optional back arrow, and pluggable link components for any router framework.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Breadcrumb stories](/story/components-breadcrumb--default) for live interactive examples.

## Variants

The Breadcrumb adapts to different navigation styles:

| Style | Separator | Back Arrow | Example |
|-------|-----------|------------|---------|
| **Web Path** | `/` | Yes | Home / Projects / **Eidotter** |
| **DOS Path** | `\` | No | C: \ DOS \ **COMMAND.COM** |
| **Custom** | Any string | Configurable | Any separator character |

```tsx
{/* Web-style navigation */}
<Breadcrumb
  trail={[
    { href: '/', label: 'Home' },
    { href: '/projects', label: 'Projects' },
  ]}
  currentLabel="Eidotter"
/>

{/* DOS-style path */}
<Breadcrumb
  trail={[
    { href: '/', label: 'C:' },
    { href: '/dos', label: 'DOS' },
  ]}
  currentLabel="COMMAND.COM"
  separator="\"
  showBackArrow={false}
/>
```

## Navigation Depth

The Breadcrumb handles various depth levels:

| Depth | Trail Items | Description |
|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Root only | 0 | Only the current label is shown, no trail |
| Single level | 1 | One parent link plus current page |
| Multi-level | 2+ | Full hierarchical path with separators |

```tsx
{/* Root only — no trail */}
<Breadcrumb trail={[]} currentLabel="Home" />

{/* Single level */}
<Breadcrumb
  trail={[{ href: '/', label: 'Home' }]}
  currentLabel="About"
/>

{/* Deep navigation */}
<Breadcrumb
  trail={[
    { href: '/', label: 'Home' },
    { href: '/projects', label: 'Projects' },
    { href: '/projects/design-systems', label: 'Design Systems' },
  ]}
  currentLabel="Eidotter"
/>
```

## States

### Back Arrow

When `showBackArrow` is true (the default), a `<` character appears before the
last trail item, indicating the nearest parent for quick back-navigation.

### Link Hover

Trail links transition from disabled text color to primary text color on hover,
animated over 150ms. The current page label always displays in primary text color
and is not a link.

### Custom Link Component

The `linkComponent` prop accepts any React component that renders an anchor-like element,
making it compatible with Next.js Link, React Router Link, or any custom routing solution.

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';

<Breadcrumb
  trail={[{ href: '/', label: 'Home' }]}
  currentLabel="Page"
  linkComponent={Link}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- **Focus visible**: 2px solid outline with 2px offset using `--color-semantic-border-focus`
- **High contrast**: Focus outline widens to 3px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: Link color transition disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA**: `<nav>` element has `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`, current page `<li>` has `aria-current="page"`, separators and back arrow are `aria-hidden="true"`
- **Semantic HTML**: Uses `<nav>` with an `<ol>` list for proper document structure
- **Keyboard**: All trail links are focusable with visible focus ring

## API Reference

### BreadcrumbProps

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `trail` | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | `[]` | Array of breadcrumb trail items (links) |
| `currentLabel` | `string` | — | Current page label (not a link) |
| `showBackArrow` | `boolean` | `true` | Show a `<` arrow on the last trail item |
| `separator` | `string` | `'/'` | Separator character between trail items |
| `linkComponent` | `React.ComponentType<{ href, className?, children }>` | — | Custom link component (e.g., Next.js Link) |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

### BreadcrumbItem

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `href` | `string` | URL or path for the breadcrumb link |
| `label` | `string` | Display text for the breadcrumb |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-text-disabled` | Trail link color and separator color |
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Hover link color and current page color |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline ring |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-family-fallback` | Fallback font family |
| `--typography-font-size-xs` | Base font size (mobile) |
| `--typography-font-size-sm` | Font size at 768px+ breakpoint |

## Origin

<ComponentOrigin name="Breadcrumb" />

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Button" />

# Button

DOS-styled action trigger with authentic CRT phosphor interaction states.

The Button is the primary interactive element in eiDotter. It uses a 4-variant system
mapped to action intent, with CGA-authentic colors and phosphor glow animations that
simulate a cold CRT monitor coming to life.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Button stories](/story/components-button--all-variants) for live interactive examples.

## Variants

Each variant maps to a specific semantic role:

| Variant | Role | Example |
|---------|------|---------|
| **Primary** | Main action, destructive confirm | Save, Delete, Submit |
| **Secondary** | Supporting action | Cancel, Back, Reset |
| **Ghost** | Tertiary / low-emphasis | Settings, More options |
| **Link** | Navigation, inline action | Learn more, View details |

```tsx
<Button variant="primary">Save Changes</Button>
<Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="ghost">Settings</Button>
<Button variant="link">Learn more</Button>
```

## Sizes

Three sizes following an 8px spacing grid:

| Size | Font | Padding | Min Height |
|------|------|---------|------------|
| `small` | 12px | 4px 8px | 24px |
| `medium` | 14px | 8px 16px | 32px |
| `large` | 16px | 12px 20px | 40px |

```tsx
<Button size="small">Small</Button>
<Button size="medium">Medium</Button>
<Button size="large">Large</Button>
```

## States

### Disabled

Reduced opacity (0.6), `not-allowed` cursor. Background forced to secondary,
text to disabled color. All variants share the same disabled appearance.

### Loading

Displays a blinking block cursor (`█`) alongside dimmed content text.
The button is functionally disabled during loading — clicks are suppressed
and `aria-disabled` is set.

### Full Width

Stretches to fill container width. Useful in modals, forms, and mobile layouts.

```tsx
<Button fullWidth>Full Width Button</Button>
```

## Interaction Design

The Primary button has a multi-layered CRT phosphor animation system:

### Rest State
Cold phosphor — no glow, no shadows. The monitor is off.

### Hover: Phosphor Warm-Up
A 3-layer box-shadow bloom builds over 400ms (`--duration-slow`):

```css
box-shadow:
  0 0 8px 0 var(--color-cga-amber-glow),    /* inner core */
  0 0 20px 2px var(--effects-phosphor-glow), /* mid bloom */
  0 0 40px 4px var(--effects-bloom-outer);   /* outer halo */
```

Text gains a subtle `text-shadow` glow. No size change — the bloom sits
entirely in box-shadow space.

### Active: Steady Energy
Background brightens to `--color-cga-amber-bright`. Glow intensifies.
A slow-crawling scanline overlay (`::after` pseudo-element) scrolls down
at 4s per cycle, simulating CRT scan refresh.

### Hover: Phosphor Warmup Flicker
On hover entry, a `phosphor-warmup` keyframe plays once (400ms). It simulates
CRT phosphor ignition: a brightness spike → overcorrection dip → secondary
excitation → settle. This runs simultaneously with the bloom transition.

### Active: Phosphor Energize Flash
On press, a `phosphor-energize` keyframe fires (150ms). A quick brightness
flash to 1.4x then holds at 1.08x while the button is held. The scanline
crawl overlay continues independently.

### Release: Power-On Impulse
On mouse-up, properties snap back with a 600ms spring curve:
`cubic-bezier(0.8, -0.5, 0.2, 1.4)`. The negative p2 creates a brief
undershoot (dips cold) and p4 > 1 overshoots past rest — a damped oscillation
that feels like phosphor decay.

### Secondary: 2-Layer Bloom

The secondary button has a softer phosphor system:

| State | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| **Hover** | 2-layer box-shadow (inner core + mid bloom), text-shadow glow, warmup flicker |
| **Active** | Intensified 2-layer glow, energize flash (no scanline) |
| **Release** | Gentler spring `cubic-bezier(0.5, -0.2, 0.2, 1.2)` over 400ms |

### Ghost: 1-Layer Bloom

The ghost button has the most minimal phosphor treatment:

| State | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| **Hover** | 1-layer box-shadow (inner core only), text-shadow glow, fast warmup (200ms) |
| **Active** | Intensified 1-layer glow, energize flash (no scanline) |
| **Release** | Subtle spring `cubic-bezier(0.5, -0.1, 0.2, 1.1)` over 300ms |

### Link: Text Glow Only

Link buttons receive only a `text-shadow` glow on hover — no box-shadow bloom
or spring easing. This keeps them lightweight for inline use.

> **Interactive comparison**: See the [PhosphorStates story](/story/components-button--phosphor-states) to compare all variants.

## Accessibility

- **Focus visible**: 2px solid outline with 2px offset, using `--color-semantic-border-focus`
- **High contrast**: Border widens to 3px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: All transitions, animations, and filters disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA**: `aria-disabled` set when disabled or loading
- **Keyboard**: Full keyboard navigation with visible focus ring

## Form Usage

Supports `type="submit"`, `type="reset"`, and `type="button"`:

```tsx
<form>
  <Button type="submit" variant="primary">Submit</Button>
  <Button type="reset" variant="secondary">Reset</Button>
  <Button type="button" variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
</form>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'link'` | `'primary'` | Visual style mapped to action intent |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | Button dimensions |
| `type` | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'` | `'button'` | HTML button type |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows block cursor loading indicator |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretches to container width |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Button label content |
| `onClick` | `(event) => void` | — | Click handler |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible label override |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-background-accent` | Primary fill |
| `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Primary text (dark on amber) |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Default border |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline |
| `--color-cga-amber-glow` | Hover glow inner core |
| `--effects-phosphor-glow` | Hover glow mid bloom |
| `--effects-bloom-outer` | Hover glow outer halo |
| `--color-cga-amber-bright` | Active state background |
| `--shadow-glow-sm` | Secondary/Ghost hover glow |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Checkbox" />

# Checkbox

DOS-styled boolean toggle using authentic bracket notation `[X]` with phosphor glow.

The Checkbox replaces the native browser checkbox with a text-based DOS representation.
Unchecked renders as `[ ]` and checked renders as `[X]` with an accent-colored phosphor
text-shadow glow. It supports both controlled and uncontrolled usage patterns.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Checkbox stories](/story/components-checkbox--all-states) for live interactive examples.

## Display

The checkbox uses pure CSS `::before` pseudo-elements to render DOS bracket notation:

| State | Display | Color |
|-------|---------|-------|
| **Unchecked** | `[ ]` | `--color-semantic-text-primary` (light gray) |
| **Checked** | `[X]` | `--color-semantic-text-accent` (amber) + phosphor glow |

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Unchecked option" />
<Checkbox label="Checked option" defaultChecked />
```

## States

### Default (Unchecked)

Displays `[ ]` in the primary text color. The label inherits the parent text color.

### Checked

Displays `[X]` in accent color with a `text-shadow: 0 0 4px` phosphor glow,
simulating the brightness of an active CRT pixel.

### Hover

When hovered (and not disabled), the box text shifts to `--color-semantic-text-secondary`,
giving a warm-up feel. This applies to both checked and unchecked states.

### Disabled

Reduced opacity (0.6) with `not-allowed` cursor. Both the box and label use
`--color-semantic-text-disabled` color. The phosphor glow is suppressed in disabled+checked state.

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Disabled" disabled />
<Checkbox label="Disabled and checked" defaultChecked disabled />
```

## Controlled vs Uncontrolled

### Controlled

Pass `checked` and `onChange` for full external state management:

```tsx
const [isEnabled, setIsEnabled] = useState(false);

<Checkbox
  label="Enable feature"
  checked={isEnabled}
  onChange={(checked) => setIsEnabled(checked)}
/>
```

### Uncontrolled

Use `defaultChecked` to set the initial state and let the checkbox manage itself:

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Remember me" defaultChecked />
```

## Form Usage

Supports standard form attributes for HTML form submission:

```tsx
<form>
  <Checkbox name="terms" value="accepted" label="I accept the terms" />
  <Checkbox name="newsletter" value="yes" label="Subscribe to newsletter" />
</form>
```

## Accessibility

- **Focus visible**: 2px solid outline with 2px offset on the box element, using `--color-semantic-border-focus`
- **High contrast**: Box gets bold weight (700), label gets semi-bold (600), focus outline widens to 3px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: Color transition on box element disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA**: Native `<input type="checkbox">` with `aria-label` falling back to `label` text
- **Keyboard**: Full keyboard navigation — native checkbox is visually hidden but remains focusable
- **Label**: Clicking the label text toggles the checkbox (wrapped in `<label>` element)

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `checked` | `boolean` | — | Controlled checked state |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | — | Initial checked state for uncontrolled usage |
| `onChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | — | Callback fired when checked state changes |
| `label` | `string` | — | Visible label text displayed next to the checkbox |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction and dims appearance |
| `name` | `string` | — | Name attribute for HTML form submission |
| `value` | `string` | — | Value attribute for HTML form submission |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible label override (defaults to `label` text) |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Unchecked box and default label color |
| `--color-semantic-text-accent` | Checked `[X]` color and phosphor glow |
| `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Hover state box color |
| `--color-semantic-text-disabled` | Disabled state box and label color |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline ring |
| `--duration-fast` | Box color transition (100ms) |
| `--spacing-2` | Gap between box and label |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-family-fallback` | Fallback font family |
| `--typography-font-size-base` | Base font size |

<Meta title="Docs/CommandPrompt" />

# CommandPrompt

DOS-styled command input with authentic terminal aesthetics and blinking block cursor.

The CommandPrompt simulates a classic DOS terminal input line. It displays a configurable
prompt string (e.g., `C:\>`), a text input, and a blinking block cursor. When the user
presses Enter, the `onCommand` callback fires with the trimmed input and the field clears.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [CommandPrompt stories](/story/components-commandprompt--default) for live interactive examples.

## Prompt Styles

The prompt string is fully configurable:

| Prompt | Style | Example |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `C:\>` | Classic DOS (default) | `C:\> dir /w` |
| `$` | Unix shell | `$ ls -la` |
| `>` | Minimal | `> help` |
| Custom | Any string | `eidotter://> scan` |

```tsx
<CommandPrompt prompt="C:\>" onCommand={handleCommand} />
<CommandPrompt prompt="$" onCommand={handleCommand} />
<CommandPrompt prompt="eidotter://>" onCommand={handleCommand} />
```

## States

### Default

Displays the prompt string, an empty input field, and a blinking block cursor (`█`).
Clicking anywhere on the container focuses the input.

### Focused

When the input is focused, the decorative block cursor hides (the browser's native
cursor takes over). The prompt string remains visible.

### Disabled

Reduced opacity (0.5), `not-allowed` cursor. The blinking cursor animation stops
and the input cannot be focused.

### With Placeholder

An optional placeholder appears in the input when empty, using the disabled text color:

```tsx
<CommandPrompt
  prompt="C:\>"
  placeholder="Type a command..."
  onCommand={handleCommand}
/>
```

## Auto-Focus

Set `autoFocus` to focus the input on mount — useful for terminal-style interfaces
where the user should immediately start typing:

```tsx
<CommandPrompt autoFocus onCommand={handleCommand} />
```

## Accessibility

- **Container role**: `role="textbox"` with `aria-label="Command prompt"`
- **Input label**: Hidden input has `aria-label="Command input"`
- **Prompt string**: Marked `aria-hidden="true"` (decorative)
- **Cursor**: Marked `aria-hidden="true"` (decorative)
- **High contrast**: Border widens to 3px, prompt text bolded, focus outline at 3px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: Blinking cursor animation disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **Keyboard**: Enter submits command, standard text input keyboard behavior

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `prompt` | `string` | `'C:\\>'` | Prompt string displayed before the input |
| `onCommand` | `(command: string) => void` | — | Callback when Enter is pressed with input text (required) |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Auto-focus input on mount |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | Placeholder text when input is empty |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-size-base` | Input font size |
| `--color-semantic-background-primary` | Container background |
| `--color-semantic-text-accent` | Container text color (amber) |
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Prompt string and input text |
| `--color-semantic-text-disabled` | Placeholder text color |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | High contrast border |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | High contrast focus outline |
| `--spacing-2` | Container padding and prompt margin |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/FilterBar" />

# FilterBar

Multi-select toggle toolbar for faceted filtering.

FilterBar renders a horizontal row of toggle buttons following the WAI-ARIA toolbar
pattern with roving tabindex. Users can activate multiple filters simultaneously.
Designed for filter UIs in Lifelines timeline and content management views.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [FilterBar stories](/story/components-filterbar--default) for live interactive examples.

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { FilterBar } from 'eidotter';

const items = [
  { id: 'all', label: 'All' },
  { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos' },
  { id: 'notes', label: 'Notes' },
];

<FilterBar
  items={items}
  activeIds={['all']}
  onToggle={(id) => toggleFilter(id)}
/>
```

## Keyboard Navigation

FilterBar implements roving tabindex per WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern:

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Arrow Right / Down | Move focus to next item |
| Arrow Left / Up | Move focus to previous item |
| Home | Move focus to first item |
| End | Move focus to last item |
| Enter / Space | Toggle active state |

Only the focused item has `tabIndex={0}`; all others have `tabIndex={-1}`.
This means Tab enters the toolbar, arrows navigate within, and Tab exits.

## Accessibility

- **Role**: `role="toolbar"` on container with `aria-label`
- **Items**: `role="button"` with `aria-pressed` for toggle state
- **Roving tabindex**: Single tab stop with arrow key navigation
- **High contrast**: 2px borders, no glow
- **Reduced motion**: Transitions disabled

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` | `FilterBarItem[]` | — | Array of `{ id, label }` toggle items |
| `activeIds` | `string[]` | `[]` | Currently active item IDs |
| `onToggle` | `(id: string) => void` | — | Called when an item is toggled |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | Button dimensions |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible toolbar label |

### FilterBarItem

```ts
interface FilterBarItem {
  id: string;
  label: string;
}
```

## Design Tokens Used

|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Item text |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Item border |
| `--color-semantic-background-accent` | Active item fill |
| `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Active item text |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline |
| `--shadow-glow-xs` | Active item glow |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Icon" />

# Icon

SVG icon component rendering from a shared spritesheet with CGA-authentic sizing.

The Icon component renders icons from `sprites.svg` using SVG `<use>` references.
Icons inherit the parent's `color` by default via `currentColor`, making them
automatically theme-aware. Interactive icons with `role="button"` gain hover effects.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Icon stories](/story/components-icon--default) for live interactive examples.

## Sizes

Two sizes optimized for DOS-style interfaces:

| Size | Dimensions | Use Case |
|------|-----------|----------|
| `L` (default) | 56 x 56px | Hero icons, feature callouts |
| `S` | 24 x 24px | Inline icons, buttons, labels |

```tsx
<Icon name="Warning" size="L" />
<Icon name="Close" size="S" />
```

## Color Override

Icons inherit `currentColor` from their parent by default. Use the `color` prop
to override with a specific token:

```tsx
{/* Inherits parent color */}
<Icon name="Check" />

{/* Explicit color override */}
<Icon name="Warning" color="var(--color-cga-bright-red)" />
<Icon name="Info" color="var(--color-semantic-text-accent)" />
```

## Interactive Icons

Add `role="button"` and `onClick` to make icons interactive. Interactive icons
gain a pointer cursor and hover color change:

```tsx
<Icon
  name="Close"
  size="S"
  role="button"
  onClick={() => handleClose()}
/>
```

## Available Icons

Icon names are derived from the `manifest.json` file. The full set is available
as the `IconName` TypeScript type, providing autocompletion in editors.

## Accessibility

- **ARIA label**: Each icon has `aria-label="{name} icon"` by default
- **Interactive icons**: `role="button"` adds keyboard and pointer semantics
- **High contrast**: Interactive icons gain a 3px focus outline via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Color inheritance**: Uses `currentColor` so icons adapt to parent text color

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `name` | `IconName` | — | Icon name from the spritesheet manifest (required) |
| `size` | `'L' \| 'S'` | `'L'` | Icon dimensions (56px or 24px) |
| `color` | `string` | — | CSS color override (inherits `currentColor` if omitted) |
| `role` | `'button'` | — | Sets interactive icon behavior |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | — | Click handler (typically paired with `role="button"`) |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Default icon color (via `currentColor`) |
| `--color-semantic-link-hover` | Hover color for interactive icons |

## Origin

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Input" />

# Input

DOS-styled text input with authentic terminal aesthetics and validation states.

The Input extends the native HTML `<input>` element, providing CGA-authentic styling
with a minimal, focused API. It uses `forwardRef` for full ref compatibility and
spreads remaining props for seamless integration with form libraries.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Input stories](/story/components-input--default) for live interactive examples.

## Variants

Each variant maps to a specific validation state:

| Variant | Role | Example |
|---------|------|---------|
| **Default** | Normal input state | Username, search, general text |
| **Error** | Invalid / failed validation | Required field missing, format error |

```tsx
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." />
<Input variant="error" placeholder="Invalid input..." />
```

## States

### Default

Standard input with `--color-semantic-border-default` border. On focus, the border
transitions to `--color-semantic-border-focus` with a subtle phosphor glow via
`--shadow-glow-sm`.

### Error

Border color changes to `--color-semantic-status-error`. The error border persists
on focus to maintain validation visibility. Sets `aria-invalid="true"` automatically.

### Disabled

Reduced opacity (0.5), `not-allowed` cursor. Background remains
`--color-semantic-background-primary` to keep the dormant terminal feel.

### Placeholder

Placeholder text uses `--color-semantic-text-disabled` for a dim, inactive appearance
that doesn't compete with entered values.

## Input Types

Supports all native HTML input types via prop spreading:

```tsx
<Input type="text" placeholder="Enter text..." />
<Input type="password" placeholder="Enter password..." />
<Input type="email" placeholder="user@example.com" />
<Input type="number" placeholder="0" />
```

## Accessibility

- **Focus visible**: Border transitions to `--color-semantic-border-focus` with phosphor glow
- **High contrast**: Border widens to 3px; focus adds a 3px solid outline with 2px offset
- **Reduced motion**: All transitions disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA**: `aria-invalid` set automatically when `variant="error"`
- **Ref forwarding**: Full `forwardRef` support for focus management and form integration

## Form Usage

Works seamlessly with native forms and form libraries:

```tsx
<form>
  <label htmlFor="username">Username</label>
  <Input id="username" name="username" required />

  <label htmlFor="password">Password</label>
  <Input id="password" name="password" type="password" />

  <Button type="submit" variant="primary">Log In</Button>
</form>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'error'` | `'default'` | Visual variant for validation states |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | Placeholder text |
| `type` | `string` | `'text'` | HTML input type (`text`, `password`, `email`, `number`, etc.) |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | — | Forwarded ref to the input element |
| `...props` | `InputHTMLAttributes` | — | All native HTML input attributes are spread |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-background-primary` | Input background |
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Input text color |
| `--color-semantic-text-disabled` | Placeholder text color |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Default border |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus border |
| `--color-semantic-status-error` | Error variant border |
| `--shadow-glow-sm` | Focus phosphor glow |
| `--border-width-medium` | Border thickness |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS monospace font |
| `--typography-font-size-base` | Input font size |
| `--spacing-2` | Input padding |
| `--duration-normal` | Border transition (200ms) |
| `--duration-slow` | Glow transition (400ms) |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin'; # Modal DOS-styled dialog overlay with CRT phosphor entrance animation and native `` semantics. The Modal uses the native HTML `` element via `showModal()` for proper focus trapping, backdrop handling, and accessibility. It portals to `document.body` to avoid stacking context issues and features a CRT-inspired entrance animation that simulates a monitor warming up. > **Interactive demos**: See the [Modal stories](/story/components-modal--default) for live interactive examples. ## Anatomy The Modal is composed of four BEM elements: | Element | Class | Purpose | |---------|-------|---------| | **Header** | `modal__header` | Title and close button row | | **Title** | `modal__title` | Yellow CGA heading text | | **Body** | `modal__body` | Scrollable content area | | **Footer** | `modal__footer` | Optional action buttons row | ```tsx setIsOpen(false)} title="Confirm Action" footer={ <> } >

Are you sure you want to proceed?

 ``` ## States ### Open When `isOpen` becomes `true`, the dialog opens via `showModal()` with a CRT phosphor entrance animation: the container scales from 0.95 with blur and reduced brightness, warming up over `--duration-slow` (400ms). The backdrop fades in over `--duration-normal` (200ms). ### Closed When `isOpen` becomes `false`, the dialog closes via `dialog.close()`. The `onOpenChange` callback fires on every state transition. ### Backdrop Clicking the backdrop (the `::backdrop` pseudo-element area) triggers `onClose`. The backdrop uses `--effects-overlay` for a semi-transparent dark overlay. ## Interaction Design ### CRT Phosphor Entrance The modal entrance simulates a cold CRT monitor powering on: ```css @keyframes modal-crt-enter { from { opacity: 0; filter: blur(4px) brightness(0.3); transform: scale(0.95); } to { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0) brightness(1); transform: scale(1); } } ``` ### Close Mechanisms Three ways to dismiss the modal: 1. **Escape key** - Native `` behavior, fires `onClose` 2. **Backdrop click** - Clicking outside the container 3. **Close button** - Icon button in the header with `aria-label="Close modal"` ## Common Patterns ### Confirmation Dialog ```tsx } >

Are you sure you want to delete this item? This action cannot be undone.

 ``` ### Form Modal ```tsx } >

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Progress" />

# Progress

DOS-themed progress bar using block characters with phosphor glow and gradient fill.

The Progress component renders a text-based progress bar using Unicode block characters
(`█` filled, `░` empty). It supports three track styles, four color variants, an
indeterminate scanning mode, and optional phosphor glow effects.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Progress stories](/story/components-progress--default) for live interactive examples.

## Track Styles

| Style | Appearance | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| `block` (default) | `[██████░░░░]` | CSS-bordered track with inset shadow |
| `bordered` | `[██████░░░░]` | Bracket characters `[` `]` as delimiters |
| `gradient` | `[██████▓▒░░]` | Smooth transition chars (`▓▒`) at fill boundary |

```tsx
<Progress value={60} trackStyle="block" />
<Progress value={60} trackStyle="bordered" />
<Progress value={60} trackStyle="gradient" />
```

## Variants

Color variants for the filled portion:

| Variant | Fill Color | Use Case |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| `default` | Primary text | General progress |
| `success` | Bright green | Completed tasks, health |
| `warning` | Yellow | Approaching limits |
| `error` | Bright red | Failures, critical |

```tsx
<Progress value={80} variant="success" />
<Progress value={50} variant="warning" />
<Progress value={20} variant="error" />
```

## Sizes

Three sizes controlling the block character font size:

| Size | Font Size | Use Case |
|------|----------|----------|
| `small` | xs (10px) | Inline, compact |
| `medium` | base (14px) | Default |
| `large` | lg (18px) | Hero, dashboard |

## Indeterminate Mode

When progress amount is unknown, a scanning block (`▓█▓`) bounces across the track:

```tsx
<Progress indeterminate showLabel />
```

The label shows `...` instead of a percentage. The scanner animation runs at 2s per cycle.

## Phosphor Glow

Enable `glow` for a CRT phosphor text-shadow effect on filled blocks:

```tsx
<Progress value={75} glow />
```

The glow adds a layered box-shadow to the track and text-shadow to fill characters.

## Full Width

Set `fullWidth` to stretch the bar across its container:

```tsx
<Progress value={45} fullWidth showLabel />
```

## Block Count

Control the number of character cells (default 20, range 3-80):

```tsx
<Progress value={50} blocks={40} />
```

## Accessibility

- **Role**: `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`
- **Indeterminate**: Omits `aria-valuenow` per WAI-ARIA spec
- **Value text**: Optional `valueText` prop for human-readable descriptions (e.g., "3 of 10 files")
- **ARIA label**: Auto-generated or custom via `aria-label`
- **High contrast**: Border widens to 3px, fill/label text bolded, glow effects disabled via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: Scanner animation disabled (parked at center), transitions removed via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | `number` | `0` | Current progress value |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | Maximum value |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Show scanning animation instead of fixed fill |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error'` | `'default'` | Fill color variant |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | Bar font size |
| `trackStyle` | `'block' \| 'bordered' \| 'gradient'` | `'block'` | Track display style |
| `blocks` | `number` | `20` | Character cell count (3-80) |
| `showLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Show percentage label |
| `glow` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable phosphor glow effect |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretch to fill container |
| `valueText` | `string` | — | Human-readable value for screen readers |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible label override |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-size-xs` | Small size |
| `--typography-font-size-base` | Medium size |
| `--typography-font-size-lg` | Large size |
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Filled blocks and label text |
| `--color-cga-brown` | Empty blocks (warm dormant phosphor) |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Track border and bracket color |
| `--color-semantic-background-secondary` | Track background |
| `--color-semantic-status-success` | Success variant fill |
| `--color-semantic-status-warning` | Warning variant fill |
| `--color-semantic-status-error` | Error variant fill |
| `--color-cga-amber-glow` | Glow inner text-shadow |
| `--effects-phosphor-glow` | Glow outer text-shadow and track shadow |
| `--effects-drop-shadow` | Track inset shadow |
| `--border-width-medium` | Track border width |
| `--opacity-50` | Gradient transition character opacity |
| `--spacing-2` | Gap between bar and label |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/RetroEffects" />

# RetroEffects

Full-screen CRT monitor overlay with scanlines, glow vignette, flicker, and phosphor bloom.

RetroEffects is a fixed-position overlay that layers authentic CRT visual effects over
your application. Each effect layer is independently toggleable. The component supports
power on/off animations that simulate a CRT monitor warming up and shutting down.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [RetroEffects stories](/story/components-retroeffects--default) for live interactive examples.

## Effect Layers

Each layer is an independently controlled overlay:

| Layer | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `scanlines` | On | Horizontal line pattern scrolling at 9s/cycle via `mix-blend-mode: screen` |
| `glow` | On | Radial vignette darkening edges, simulating phosphor falloff |
| `flicker` | On | Subtle opacity oscillation at 2Hz (WCAG 2.3.1 compliant, under 3Hz threshold) |
| `bloom` | Off | Soft inner glow simulating CRT halation (opt-in for performance) |

```tsx
{/* All default effects */}
<RetroEffects />

{/* Selective layers */}
<RetroEffects scanlines glow flicker={false} bloom />

{/* Minimal — scanlines only */}
<RetroEffects glow={false} flicker={false} />
```

## Intensity

The `intensity` prop (0-1) scales all effect opacities proportionally via the
`--retro-intensity` CSS custom property:

```tsx
<RetroEffects intensity={0.5} />  {/* Half strength */}
<RetroEffects intensity={0.2} />  {/* Subtle hint */}
```

## Power Animations

Toggle `powered` to trigger CRT power on/off animations:

### Power On (600ms ease-out)
Horizontal line expands to full screen, simulating a CRT warming up from cold.

### Power Off (400ms ease-in)
Screen collapses to a horizontal line then disappears, simulating CRT shutdown.

```tsx
const [powered, setPowered] = useState(true);

<RetroEffects
  powered={powered}
  onPowerOn={() => console.log('CRT warm')}
  onPowerOff={() => console.log('CRT cold')}
  onPowerStateChange={(state) => console.log(state)}
/>
```

### Power State Machine

The component tracks four states: `on`, `powering-on`, `powering-off`, `off`.
The `onPowerStateChange` callback fires on each transition. Children are hidden
when fully `off`.

## Accessibility

- **ARIA hidden**: Entire component is `aria-hidden="true"` (purely decorative)
- **Pointer events**: Set to `none` — effects never block interaction
- **Flicker safety**: Oscillation at 2Hz, well under the WCAG 2.3.1 three-flash threshold
- **High contrast**: Entire component is `display: none` via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: All animations disabled. Power transitions replaced with simple opacity fades (0.2s off, 0.3s on) via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `scanlines` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable scanline overlay |
| `glow` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable vignette glow |
| `flicker` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable CRT flicker |
| `bloom` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable phosphor bloom (opt-in) |
| `powered` | `boolean` | `true` | CRT power state (animates transitions) |
| `intensity` | `number` | `1` | Effect intensity (0-1) |
| `onPowerStateChange` | `(state: PowerState) => void` | — | Fires on power state transitions |
| `onPowerOn` | `() => void` | — | Fires when power-on animation completes |
| `onPowerOff` | `() => void` | — | Fires when power-off animation completes |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

### PowerState Type

```ts
type PowerState = 'on' | 'powering-on' | 'powering-off' | 'off';
```

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--effects-scanline-light` | Scanline light band |
| `--effects-scanline-dark` | Scanline dark band |
| `--effects-vignette-glow` | Glow vignette inner shadow |
| `--effects-vignette-edge` | Vignette gradient edge |
| `--effects-vignette-corner` | Vignette gradient corner |
| `--effects-screen-tint` | Flicker background tint |
| `--effects-phosphor-glow` | Bloom inner glow |
| `--effects-bloom-outer` | Bloom outer halo |
| `--effects-bloom-center` | Bloom radial gradient center |
| `--duration-power-on` | Power-on animation duration (600ms fallback) |
| `--duration-power-off` | Power-off animation duration (400ms fallback) |

## Origin

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Tabs" />

# Tabs

DOS-styled tab navigation with underline and pills variants for content switching.

The Tabs component provides keyboard-navigable tab selection with two visual variants,
three sizes, and support for both controlled and uncontrolled modes. Tabs use uppercase
CGA-authentic labels with phosphor text-shadow effects on hover.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Tabs stories](/story/components-tabs--default) for live interactive examples.

## Variants

Each variant maps to a different navigation context:

| Variant | Style | Use Case |
|---------|-------|----------|
| **Underline** | Bottom border indicator | Content switching, minimal UI |
| **Pills** | Contained background fill | App navigation, toolbar mode selection |

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={tabs} variant="underline" />
<Tabs tabs={tabs} variant="pills" />
```

## Sizes

Three sizes following an 8px spacing grid:

| Size | Font | Padding (Underline) | Padding (Pills) |
|------|------|---------------------|-----------------|
| `small` | 10px | 4px 10px | 4px 8px |
| `medium` | 12px | 8px 16px | 6px 12px |
| `large` | 14px | 10px 20px | 8px 16px |

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={tabs} size="small" />
<Tabs tabs={tabs} size="medium" />
<Tabs tabs={tabs} size="large" />
```

## States

### Active Tab

The active tab has full opacity. In underline variant, it gains a bottom border
in the accent color. In pills variant, it fills with the accent background and
switches to secondary (dark) text.

### Inactive Tab

Inactive tabs render at 0.7 opacity (tuned for WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast ratio).
On hover, opacity returns to 1 and a subtle `text-shadow` glow appears.

### Disabled Tab

Disabled tabs render at 0.3 opacity with `not-allowed` cursor. They are skipped
during keyboard navigation and cannot be activated.

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={[
  { id: 'active', label: 'Active' },
  { id: 'disabled', label: 'Disabled', disabled: true },
  { id: 'another', label: 'Another' },
]} />
```

## Controlled vs Uncontrolled

### Uncontrolled (default)

Use `defaultActiveTab` to set the initial tab. The component manages its own state:

```tsx
<Tabs
  tabs={tabs}
  defaultActiveTab="schedule"
  onTabChange={(tabId, previousTabId) => console.log(tabId, previousTabId)}
/>
```

### Controlled

Pass `activeTab` and `onTabChange` for full external control:

```tsx
const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState('schedule');
<Tabs tabs={tabs} activeTab={activeTab} onTabChange={setActiveTab} />
```

## Tab Items

Tabs are defined as an array of `TabItem` objects:

```tsx
interface TabItem {
  id: string;       // Unique identifier
  label: string;    // Display label
  disabled?: boolean; // Whether the tab is disabled
}

const tabs = [
  { id: 'schedule', label: 'Schedule' },
  { id: 'ai', label: 'AI Console' },
  { id: 'calendars', label: 'Calendars' },
];
```

## Keyboard Navigation

The Tabs component implements the WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern:

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowUp` | Move to previous enabled tab |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowDown` | Move to next enabled tab |
| `Home` | Move to first enabled tab |
| `End` | Move to last enabled tab |

Navigation wraps around: pressing ArrowRight on the last tab moves to the first.

## Accessibility

- **Role**: `tablist` container with `tab` role on each button
- **ARIA selected**: `aria-selected` reflects active state
- **Tab index**: Active tab is `tabIndex={0}`, inactive tabs are `tabIndex={-1}` (roving tabindex)
- **Focus visible**: 2px solid outline with 2px offset, using `--color-semantic-border-focus`
- **High contrast**: Underline border widens to 3px, pills container border widens to 2px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: All transitions disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **ARIA label**: Supports `aria-label` on the tab list for context (e.g., "Main navigation")

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `tabs` | `TabItem[]` | — | Array of tab items to display (required) |
| `variant` | `'underline' \| 'pills'` | `'underline'` | Visual style of the tabs |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | Tab dimensions |
| `activeTab` | `string` | — | Controlled active tab ID |
| `defaultActiveTab` | `string` | — | Initial active tab ID (uncontrolled) |
| `onTabChange` | `(tabId: string, previousTabId: string) => void` | — | Callback when active tab changes |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible label for the tab list |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Inactive tab text |
| `--color-semantic-text-accent` | Active underline tab text and border |
| `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Active pills tab text (dark on amber) |
| `--color-semantic-background-secondary` | Pills container background |
| `--color-semantic-background-accent` | Active pills tab fill |
| `--color-semantic-background-primary` | Pills tab hover background |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Underline hover border, pills container border |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | DOS font family |
| `--typography-font-weight-regular` | Tab label weight |
| `--duration-fast` | Transition speed (100ms) |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin';

<Meta title="Docs/Tag" />

# Tag

Interactive label component for tags, categories, and filter chips.

Tag extends Badge's display-only approach with click, close, and selection behaviors.
Use for content labels users can add, remove, click, or toggle. TagGroup provides
consistent spacing when rendering multiple tags together.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [Tag stories](/story/components-tag--default) for live interactive examples.

## Tag vs Badge

| Concern | Badge | Tag |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Purpose | Status indicator | Content label |
| Interactive | No | Yes (click, close, select) |
| Element | `<span>` | `<span>` with optional `role="button"` |
| Focusable | No | Yes (when interactive) |
| Removable | No | Yes (optional close button) |

## Variants

| Variant | Visual | Use case |
|---------|--------|----------|
| `default` | Subtle border, transparent bg | General purpose tags |
| `outlined` | Colored border and text | Category indicators with custom color |
| `filled` | Colored background, dark text | High-emphasis labels like PARA categories |

```tsx
<Tag variant="default">general</Tag>
<Tag variant="outlined" color="--color-cga-bright-cyan">project</Tag>
<Tag variant="filled" color="--color-cga-bright-green">area</Tag>
```

## Close Button

The `closeable` prop adds a DOS-authentic `[x]` button. The close button uses
`tabIndex={-1}` so focus stays on the tag body; pressing Delete or Backspace
triggers close from the tag itself.

```tsx
<Tag closeable onClose={(e) => handleRemove()}>removable</Tag>
```

## Selected State

Toggle `selected` to show an active/filled appearance with a glow shadow.
Combine with `onClick` for filter chip behavior.

```tsx
<Tag selected={isActive} onClick={() => toggleFilter()}>
  filter
</Tag>
```

## Custom Colors

The `color` prop accepts a CSS custom property name and sets `--tag-color` on the
element. Both `outlined` and `filled` variants respond to this property.

```tsx
const paraColors = {
  project: '--color-cga-bright-cyan',
  area: '--color-cga-bright-green',
  resource: '--color-cga-yellow',
  archive: '--color-cga-brown',
};

<Tag variant="filled" color={paraColors[entry.para]}>
  {entry.para}
</Tag>
```

## TagGroup

Wraps multiple tags with consistent flex spacing and optional line wrapping.

```tsx
<TagGroup gap="tight">
  {tags.map(t => <Tag key={t} closeable onClose={() => remove(t)}>{t}</Tag>)}
</TagGroup>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `gap` | `'tight' \| 'normal' \| 'loose'` | `'normal'` | Spacing between tags (4px/8px/12px) |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `true` | Wrap to multiple lines |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible group label |

## Keyboard Interaction

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Enter / Space | Trigger `onClick` (when interactive) |
| Delete / Backspace | Trigger `onClose` (when closeable) |

## Accessibility

- **Role**: `role="button"` and `tabIndex={0}` when `onClick` is provided
- **Selected**: `aria-selected` set when `selected` is true
- **Disabled**: `aria-disabled` set, pointer events disabled
- **Close button**: `aria-label="Remove {label}"`, `tabIndex={-1}`
- **TagGroup**: `role="group"` with `aria-label`
- **High contrast**: Border widens to 2px, glow removed
- **Reduced motion**: All transitions disabled

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Tag display text |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'outlined' \| 'filled'` | `'default'` | Visual variant |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | Tag dimensions |
| `color` | `string` | — | CGA color token (e.g. `'--color-cga-bright-cyan'`) |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Active/selected state |
| `closeable` | `boolean` | `false` | Show `[x]` close button |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable all interaction |
| `onClick` | `(event) => void` | — | Click handler (makes tag interactive) |
| `onClose` | `(event) => void` | — | Close handler |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible label override |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Default text color |
| `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Filled variant text |
| `--color-semantic-border-default` | Default border |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline |
| `--color-semantic-background-accent` | Selected/filled background |
| `--shadow-glow-xs` | Selected and hover glow |

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import { ComponentOrigin } from '@/docs/ComponentOrigin'; # Terminal DOS-styled window frame with title bar, window controls, and content area. The Terminal component recreates the classic MS-DOS/Windows 3.x window chrome with an authentic title bar, minimize/maximize/close controls, and a content area with a blinking block cursor. It supports three sizes, active/inactive/minimized states, and a maximized mode that fills the viewport. > **Interactive demos**: See the [Terminal stories](/story/components-terminal--default) for live interactive examples. ## Sizes Three preset sizes modeled after classic DOS display resolutions: | Size | Width | Height | |------|-------|--------| | `small` | 480px | 320px | | `medium` | 640px | 480px | | `large` | 800px | 600px | ```tsx ``` ## States ### Active The title bar fills with the accent background color (amber). The window border uses the secondary text color for a prominent, focused appearance. ### Inactive The title bar falls back to the secondary background with primary text color. The border dims to the disabled text color, indicating the window does not have focus. ### Minimized The window content collapses and a taskbar item is rendered instead, showing the app icon and title. Clicking or pressing Enter on the taskbar item restores the window to active state. ### Maximized Toggled via the maximize control. The window expands to fill the entire viewport (`100vw x 100vh`) with `position: fixed`, border and box-shadow removed, at `z-index: 1000`. ```tsx ``` ## Window Controls Each control button can be independently enabled or disabled: | Control | Default | Description | |---------|---------|-------------| | `minimizable` | `true` | Shows minimize button, collapses to taskbar | | `maximizable` | `true` | Shows maximize/restore button | | `closeable` | `true` | Shows close button | | `resizable` | `true` | Shows resize handle in bottom-right corner | ```tsx ``` ## Custom Content Pass children to replace the default prompt display: ```tsx
{`C:\\>dir 3 file(s) 54,813 bytes C:\\>`} █
``` When no children are provided, the Terminal renders a default `C:\>` prompt with a blinking block cursor. ## Interaction Design ### Title Bar The title bar displays an app icon and title text. It uses `user-select: none` and `cursor: default` to simulate classic window chrome that cannot be text-selected. ### Control Buttons Window control buttons invert their colors on `:active` using `filter: invert(1)`, replicating the classic DOS button press feedback. Each button has an accessible `aria-label` and `title` attribute. ### Keyboard Shortcuts - **Alt+F4**: Closes the terminal (when `closeable` is `true`) - **Enter** on minimized taskbar item: Restores the window ## Accessibility - **Role**: Uses `role="dialog"` with `aria-label` describing the window - **Minimized role**: Taskbar item uses `role="button"` with `aria-label` for restore action - **Window controls**: Each control button has descriptive `aria-label` (e.g., "Minimize window") - **Focus management**: `tabIndex={0}` on the window, `autoFocus` option for mount focus - **High contrast**: Border widens to 3px, control borders to 2px, focus outline to 3px via `prefers-contrast: high` - **Reduced motion**: Cursor blink animation disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` - **Content area**: Uses `role="main"` for the terminal content region ## API Reference | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | Window dimensions | | `title` | `string` | `'MS-DOS Terminal'` | Title bar text | | `state` | `'active' \| 'inactive' \| 'minimized'` | `'active'` | Initial window state | | `resizable` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows resize handle | | `minimizable` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows minimize control | | `maximizable` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows maximize control | | `closeable` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows close control | | `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Terminal content (replaces default prompt) | | `onMinimize` | `() => void` | — | Callback when minimized | | `onMaximize` | `() => void` | — | Callback when maximized/restored | | `onClose` | `() => void` | — | Callback when closed | | `onFocus` | `() => void` | — | Callback when window gains focus | | `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes | | `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Auto-focus on mount | ## Design Tokens Used | Token | Purpose | |-------|---------| | `--color-semantic-background-primary` | Window background, control symbol color | | `--color-semantic-background-secondary` | Title bar background (inactive) | | `--color-semantic-background-accent` | Title bar background (active) | | `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Content text, control button background | | `--color-semantic-text-secondary` | Title bar text (active) | | `--color-semantic-text-disabled` | Window border (inactive) | | `--color-semantic-border-focus` | High contrast focus outline | | `--effects-drop-shadow` | DOS-style box shadow (5px 5px) | ## Origin

# TimelineNode

Axis marker for timeline and stepper interfaces with CGA amber phosphor glow.

TimelineNode is a versatile marker component for timelines, steppers, and progress
indicators. It supports three shapes, four color variants, optional labels with
configurable position, and amber phosphor glow effects on hover and active states.

> **Interactive demos**: See the [TimelineNode stories](/story/components-timelinenode--default) for live interactive examples.

## Shapes

| Shape | Appearance | CSS |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| `circle` (default) | Round marker | `border-radius: 50%` |
| `square` | Rounded square | `border-radius: 2px` |
| `diamond` | Rotated square | `transform: rotate(45deg)` |

```tsx
<TimelineNode shape="circle" />
<TimelineNode shape="square" />
<TimelineNode shape="diamond" />
```

## Variants

Four color variants for the marker fill and border:

| Variant | Color | Use Case |
|---------|-------|----------|
| `default` | Amber dim | Inactive/past events |
| `primary` | Amber | Current/important events |
| `secondary` | Primary text | Neutral markers |
| `accent` | Accent text | Highlighted events |

```tsx
<TimelineNode variant="default" />
<TimelineNode variant="primary" />
<TimelineNode variant="secondary" />
<TimelineNode variant="accent" />
```

## Sizes

| Size | Marker | Diamond | Use Case |
|------|--------|---------|----------|
| `small` | 8px | 7px | Compact timelines |
| `medium` | 12px | 10px | Default |
| `large` | 16px | 14px | Hero timelines |

## Labels

Optional text labels with four position options:

```tsx
<TimelineNode label="Jan 2026" labelPosition="left" />
<TimelineNode label="Jan 2026" labelPosition="right" />
<TimelineNode label="Jan 2026" labelPosition="top" />
<TimelineNode label="Jan 2026" labelPosition="bottom" />
```

Label font size scales with node size: 10px for small, xs for medium, sm for large.

## Active State

The `isActive` prop highlights the node with a brighter amber fill and phosphor glow:

```tsx
<TimelineNode isActive variant="primary" label="Now" />
```

Active + interactive nodes gain a stronger glow (`--shadow-glow-md`) on hover.

## Interactive Nodes

Add `onClick` to make nodes clickable. Interactive nodes gain pointer cursor,
hover glow, keyboard support, and `role="button"` with `aria-pressed`:

```tsx
<TimelineNode
  label="Step 1"
  onClick={() => goToStep(1)}
  isActive={currentStep === 1}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- **Interactive role**: `role="button"` with `tabIndex={0}` when `onClick` is provided
- **Active state**: `aria-pressed` reflects `isActive` on interactive nodes
- **Focus visible**: 2px solid outline with 2px offset using `--color-semantic-border-focus`
- **High contrast**: Marker border widens to 3px, focus outline widens to 3px via `prefers-contrast: high`
- **Reduced motion**: All transitions disabled via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- **Keyboard**: Enter and Space activate interactive nodes

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `shape` | `'circle' \| 'square' \| 'diamond'` | `'circle'` | Marker shape |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'accent'` | `'default'` | Color variant |
| `isActive` | `boolean` | `false` | Active/selected state with glow |
| `label` | `string` | — | Optional label text |
| `labelPosition` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom'` | `'left'` | Label placement relative to marker |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | Marker dimensions |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | — | Click handler (enables interactive mode) |
| `className` | `string` | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

## Design Tokens Used

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `--color-cga-amber-dim` | Default variant fill and border |
| `--color-cga-amber` | Primary variant fill, hover state, label text |
| `--color-cga-amber-bright` | Active state fill |
| `--color-semantic-text-primary` | Secondary variant fill |
| `--color-semantic-text-accent` | Accent variant fill |
| `--color-semantic-border-focus` | Focus outline color |
| `--shadow-glow-sm` | Hover and active glow |
| `--shadow-glow-md` | Active + hover glow |
| `--typography-font-family-primary` | Label font family |
| `--typography-font-size-xs` | Medium label font size |
| `--typography-font-size-sm` | Large label font size |
| `--spacing-2` | Gap between marker and label |
